questions.question: Meeting summaries arrived as three customer requests. Large-workspace slowness arrived from monitoring, with no support tickets ever mentioning speed. What does the ticket silence justify concluding about priority?
options: Meeting summaries are the higher priority, because demonstrated demand beats an internal metric
Nothing on its own — severity and visibility are independent, and a slow product is a problem people usually act on by using it less rather than by complaining
Slowness is the higher priority, because silent problems are always the dangerous ones
Both should be deprioritised until the team can collect comparable evidence for each
questions.explanation: Channels measure visibility, not severity, so silence cannot be read as low severity or as high severity by itself. A is the tempting distractor and the one most teams pick: it treats request volume as demand evidence, when requests only reach you from customers who have a path to your inbox and expect asking to work.

questions.question: A PM scores five opportunities on reach, impact, confidence and effort, multiplies, and ranks them. What is the core defect?
options: The four factors should be weighted, since impact matters more than effort
Confidence should be assessed after the ranking, not inside it
The inputs are estimates in incompatible units, so the product is a comparable number with no meaning — and the debate moves to whether impact is a 3 or a 4
Five opportunities is too few for a scoring model to discriminate usefully
questions.explanation: Multiplying incommensurable estimates launders assumptions into something that looks like analysis, and the resulting argument cannot be won or learned from. A is the tempting distractor because adding weights is the standard fix teams reach for, and it makes the false comparability worse rather than better.

questions.question: Enterprise team leads currently paste meeting notes into a document and tidy them afterwards. How does this change the size of the meeting-summaries opportunity?
options: It confirms the opportunity, since the manual workaround proves the need is real
It has no effect on size; the workaround is evidence of the problem, not of its value
It shrinks it to the gain over the workaround — and if the workaround is adequate, that gain may be small enough to change the ordering
It enlarges it, because the manual effort can be counted as time saved per meeting
questions.explanation: Value is the improvement over what people do today, not the whole problem. A is the tempting distractor because a workaround genuinely does confirm the behaviour exists — it establishes reality and simultaneously caps the gain, and teams reliably take the first half and drop the second.

questions.question: A core dependency loses support in ten weeks. Where does it belong in the comparison?
options: Subtracted first as a constraint on capacity, because it has no alternative and its consequence appears only past a threshold
Ranked at the top, since regulatory and security work always outranks feature work
Ranked normally on the five tests, with urgency raising its consequence score
Excluded from product prioritisation entirely, as an engineering matter
questions.explanation: Forced choices do not compete with opportunities; they reduce the capacity that opportunities are being ranked against. C is the tempting distractor because running the tests feels even-handed, but the alternatives row is empty by definition and the consequence row is a step function, so the scores it produces are not comparable with anything.

questions.question: Investigation suggests large-workspace slowness and enterprise dissatisfaction may both stem from the same permission-checking behaviour. What does this do to the comparison?
options: It strengthens the case for meeting summaries, since one build would address two signals
It changes nothing; the two signals still consume separate engineering capacity
It raises confidence in both consequence chains, so both should move up the ordering together
It makes ranking them against each other the wrong shape — they may be complements, so the shared mechanism has to be resolved before any comparison is meaningful
questions.explanation: The five tests assume opportunities are substitutes competing for capacity. A shared mechanism breaks that assumption: solving one may shrink or remove the other. A is the tempting distractor because it reaches the right observation and draws the wrong conclusion — a shared mechanism argues for fixing the mechanism, not for building the feature that sat on top of it.
